title: `clamp` has zero derivative with respect to `max` where `x <= max < min`, although its result is `max`
description: `lax.clamp(min, x, max)` lowers to StableHLO `clamp`, which computes `minimum(maximum(x, min), max)`.
So where `min > max`, the result is `max` for every `x`,
and near a point with `x < max < min` the function is just `max`, with derivative 1 with respect to `max`.
Forward and reverse mode return 0 instead.
`jnp.clip`, which is built from `maximum` and `minimum`, gets the derivative right.
**Cause.** The rule for `min` guards against `min > max` with `lt(min, max)`, so it correctly returns 0 there.
The rule for `max`, `select(lt(max, operand), g, _zeros(operand))`, has no such guard:
it returns the tangent of `max` only where `max < x`.
So where `x < max < min`, every rule returns 0.
**Lean.** `Jax.Lax.clampJvp_correct` proves the three rules correct where every entry has
`x > max`, or `min < x < max`, or `x < min < max`.
At every other point where `clamp` is differentiable, some entry has `x <= max < min`, and the rules are wrong there.
The docstring of `lax.clamp` says the result is `min` where `x < min`, which disagrees with XLA where `min > max`.
reproducer: # XLA computes minimum(maximum(x, lo), hi), so with lo > hi the result is hi, also near the point.
print(lax.clamp(lo, x, hi - 1e-3), lax.clamp(lo, x, hi + 1e-3))
# So the derivative is 1 in hi and 0 in x and lo, as jnp.clip computes.
# The rule of lax.clamp for hi returns 0, because hi < x is false.
# The same at x = hi < lo, where the result is hi too.
